clue.text: Former Taoiseach said personal security guard is key individual

indicators.note: said signals that we want a word sounding like the former Irish leader's surname, not its spelling

parts.note: Jack Lynch was Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) in the 1960s and 1970s
a PIN, personal identification number, guards your bank card

explanation.surface: A former Irish prime minister supposedly called his bodyguard the most important person around.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the Irish prime minister; LYNCH said out loud gives LINCH. 'Personal security guard' reads as a bodyguard but is the PIN that protects a card.
explanation.definitionFit: A linchpin is literally the pin holding a wheel on, figuratively the person everything depends on.

clue.text: Sort of secrets revealed in Monsters, Inc., each detailed crudely

indicators.note: done crudely, the letters are knocked roughly into a new order
each of the two words loses its tail, its final letter

explanation.surface: Hidden truths come out in the animated film Monsters, Inc., each spelt out rather vulgarly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each detailed' cuts the last letter from both words, leaving MONSTER and IN; 'crudely' then rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost secrets are the most private ones, so the word describes a kind of secret.

clue.text: Catch hold of head of cobra (large snake)

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
an asp is a venomous snake, Cleopatra's

explanation.surface: Grab a big snake by its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp something is to grip or seize it tightly in the hand.

clue.text: Rip up root, for mixing into a stew

indicators.note: letters taken for mixing are stirred into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: tear up a root vegetable and stir it into the stewpot.
explanation.walkthrough: The French original means a 'rotten pot', a dish of mixed meats and vegetables, before it came to mean scented dried petals.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase first named a stew of assorted meats, hence any medley.

clue.text: Ancient city in former British colony is not affected

indicators.note: the city is placed in the colony, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Natal was a British colony in southern Africa, now KwaZulu-Natal
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city of the Bible

explanation.surface: An ancient city sitting within an old colony has stayed untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone natural in manner is unaffected, free of pretence or airs.

clue.text: Like the tail of a duck — tail removed, sadly, by gangster

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or messily, so the letters are jumbled
the word duck has its last letter cut off

parts.note: Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster

explanation.surface: A duck has lost its tail, sadly, at the hands of a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail removed' signals the cut and 'sadly' the shuffle; the duck here is not a whole bird but fodder for the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Caudal is the zoological adjective meaning relating to or resembling a tail.

clue.text: Doctor put in key order for memory device

indicators.note: the doctor is put in, placed inside the other letters

parts.note: C is a musical key
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A medic installed in a key position sorts out a storage gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact disc that can only be read stores data, a kind of computer memory medium.

clue.text: Form of investment providing one with credit

parts.note: a unit is a single one
to give credit is to trust or believe

explanation.surface: An investment product that offers a person credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pooled fund in which investors buy units is a common British savings vehicle.

clue.text: Dispense a large amount to be taken orally

indicators.note: medicine-label phrasing for spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: a lot means a large amount

explanation.surface: A pharmacist hands out a big dose of medicine to be swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares, as one dispenses portions.

clue.text: Ref let banter in game become subject of controversy?

indicators.note: game here means willing or up for anything, so the letters are shuffled freely

explanation.surface: A referee who allows taunting during a match finds himself at the centre of a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the match, but as an adjective it is the anagram signal. The question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for an unruly child describes a shocking, unconventional figure who provokes outrage.

clue.text: See 9
Sob quietly in front of flipping French girl's coded text

indicators.note: the first pieces sit in front of the rest

parts.note: to sob is to cry
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly

indicators.note: flipping turns the name over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Margot is a French girl's name; the 's is is

explanation.surface: Someone weeps softly before a French girl's maddening message.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a piece of writing in cipher or code.

clue.text: A Farewell to Arms, just opened twice

indicators.note: the letters picked are used two times over
only the openings, the first letters, of the words are taken

explanation.surface: Hemingway's novel A Farewell to Arms, barely begun two times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Farewell to Arms' is Hemingway's novel; the initials of 'to Arms' are written out twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: The woman's after a small child? Not this one!

indicators.note: the woman's word comes after the child

parts.note: a tot is a toddler
her is the woman; 's is is

explanation.surface: A mother chasing a toddler insists she wants a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect for the other, the alternative to the item in front of you.

clue.text: Carefully selects journalists embracing new measure of resolution

indicators.note: the journalists hold the other letters in their embrace

parts.note: hacks are journalists, often disparagingly
dpi, dots per inch, measures print or screen resolution

explanation.surface: Reporters adopt a fresh standard for image quality and choose with care.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand-pick is to choose personally and with great care.

clue.text: The FT's in party queen's hand

parts.note: Labour is the UK's main left-of-centre political party
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen; 's is is

explanation.surface: The Financial Times finds itself in the grip of a political party's queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand, and so is a labourer.

clue.text: Reckless gambles involving a league that includes Rugby and Poole, we hear

definitions.note: Rugby and Poole are English towns; Poole sounds like polo, and rugby and polo are sports with balls

indicators.note: reckless means wild, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Wild bets placed in a league featuring the towns of Rugby and Poole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involving' just links the gambles to the extra letters. Rugby is a Warwickshire town and Poole a Dorset port; said, Poole is polo.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby and polo are both sports played with a ball, examples of the category.

clue.text: Soothing girlfriend of gangster that is found in e-books

indicators.note: the pieces are found in, inside, the e-books letters

parts.note: E for electronic plus NT, the New Testament books
a moll is a gangster's girlfriend
i.e. is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A mobster's soothing girlfriend appears in digital books.
explanation.definitionFit: An emollient cream softens and calms the skin; figuratively, calming or placatory.

clue.text: Implements production of tinsel in America

indicators.note: the reworked letters sit in the country's abbreviation

parts.note: US, United States

indicators.note: a production is a making or staging, so the letters are refashioned

explanation.surface: Carries out the making of Christmas decorations in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implements' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Utensils are tools or implements, especially kitchen ones.

clue.text: Laugh about German shorts' turn- up

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up flips the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning
gins are short drinks, spirits

explanation.surface: A chuckle at a German's shorts with turn-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A snigger is a sly, half-suppressed laugh.

clue.text: Skin care product? Spot's about gone!

indicators.note: with the about word gone, its letters are removed

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: Delight that a pimple has nearly cleared up, thanks to some cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a pimple but means a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a liquid preparation applied to the skin.

clue.text: Small number to enter the Philippines, as the French request

indicators.note: the small number goes in, entering the country code

parts.note: RP, Republic of the Philippines, its international vehicle code
S is small
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A small group arriving in the Philippines follows French protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: The initials stand for répondez s'il vous plaît, a French plea for a reply.

clue.text: This shifted fencing by a fraction

indicators.note: the rearranged letters fence in, enclose, the by letter
shifted means moved about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: x as in two by four, the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: This was moved, enclosing an area by a small amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shifted' turns THIS into SITH, which encloses X.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth is one of six equal parts, a simple fraction.

clue.text: B—– large bed, I suspect — if so, you can make the other side!

definitions.text: if so, you can make the other side!

parts.note: the censored expletive leaves only its initial letter

indicators.note: suspect, as an adjective, means dubious, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An exasperated sleeper suspects a huge bed can be crossed, if only just.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes hide a rude word, leaving B to join LARGE BED I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bridgeable can be spanned, so you are able to reach the far side.

clue.text: One who scored ecstasy

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ..., English composer and Master of the Queen's Music, wrote film scores

explanation.surface: A goalscorer in raptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect joy, and also the surname of the composer Sir Arthur, who wrote musical scores.

clue.text: Corridor in which Liverpool manager once stripped off

indicators.note: the name has its outer letters peeled off

parts.note: Bob Paisley managed Liverpool FC from 1974 to 1983

explanation.surface: A former football boss undressed in a passageway.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, a kind of corridor.

clue.text: Former luvvie's job in sort of firm that's hard to please

parts.note: ex means former
a luvvie is a gushing theatrical type, whose job is acting

explanation.surface: An ex-actor's job at a firm with a demanding boss.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvie is British slang for an effusive actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting person is demanding, insisting on high standards.

clue.text: Become an expert in how a term's evolved?

indicators.note: letters that have evolved have changed into a new form

explanation.surface: Studying how a word developed is the route to real knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To master a subject is to learn it thoroughly, gaining full skill.

clue.text: Monkey King, in Greek mythology

definitions.meaning: the Thracian king killed by Diomedes and Odysseus at Troy in the Iliad

explanation.surface: A monkey king from Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an Asian macaque and the Thracian ruler slain in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Pays proper attention to details

definitions.meaning: honours or heeds, as one does with someone's wishes

explanation.surface: Someone attends dutifully to the fine print.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to honour or heed; as a plural noun, particular points of a matter.
